extracted.intended_audience: agency human resources officials (CHCOs), agency leadership, federal HR practitioners, agency legal counsel, and stakeholders affected by moves between competitive and excepted service
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedures and standards agencies must follow when moving positions or employees from the competitive service to the excepted service, or between excepted service schedules, including documentation, CHCO certification, OPM approval, notice rights, and MSPB appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify types, numbers, and locations of positions/employees proposed to move
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must "Identify the types, numbers, and locations of the employee(s) or position(s) that the agency proposes to move into or within the excepted service." (listed as procedural requirement 1 and echoed in §302.602(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a directive explicitly delineates positions, the agency need only list those positions and their location in the organization (§302.602(a)(1)). If the directive requires selection pursuant to articulated criteria or confers discretion, see related requirements to provide criteria, explanations, and lists (§302.602(a)(2)-(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document basis that movement is consistent with applicable standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must "Document the basis for its determination that movement of the employee(s) or position(s) is consistent with the standards set forth by the President, Congress, OPM, or their designees, as applicable." (procedural requirement 2; §302.602(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should explain how the move meets the standards in the directive or statute; OPM may request explanations. OPM declined to mandate a specific report format but may provide templates or guidance later.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHCO certification of sufficiency and merit-system consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must "Obtain certification from the agency's Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO) that the documentation is sufficient and movement of the employee(s) or position(s) is both consistent with the standards ... and advances sound merit system principles." (procedural requirement 3; §302.602(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM explains CHCOs are statutorily responsible for implementing civil service rules and are well positioned to certify sufficiency. OPM will not shift this duty to Department-level HR or OPM absent further rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit CHCO certification and supporting documentation to OPM in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must "Submit the CHCO certification and supporting documentation to OPM (to include the types, numbers, and locations of the employee(s) or position(s)) in advance of using the excepted service authority." (procedural requirement 4; §302.602(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission is required before using the excepted authority; OPM believes reporting is implicit in the CHCO certification but may later provide further instructions/templates on the forms this information should take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain written approval from OPM Director before using excepted service authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may "use the excepted service authority only after obtaining written approval from the OPM Director to do so." (procedural requirement 5; §302.602(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will review the CHCO certification and supporting documentation and provide written authorization; agencies must wait for that written approval before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM must publish authorizations in the Federal Register before hiring under the authority
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM shall "publish any such authorizations in the Federal Register, to include the types, numbers, and locations of the positions moved to the excepted service" and agencies shall not "initiate any hiring actions under the excepted service authority until such publication occurs." (procedural requirement 6; §302.602(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is intended to increase transparency. OPM declined suggestions to require public comment on such publications or to make personnel actions ineffective until 90 days after release; it considers the Federal Register publication sufficient and public comment unduly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope covers both positions and encumbered employees (including involuntary moves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart F applies to "(1) a position from the competitive service to the excepted service, or between excepted services ...; or (2) an employee who has accrued status and civil service protections ... involuntarily to any position that is not covered by that chapter or subchapter." (§302.601 revised language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM clarifies coverage of both positions and employees because incumbents acquire rights over time; the rule applies to involuntary movements and also to cases where a position becomes governed by a different title of the U.S. Code, unless otherwise provided by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply this subpart even when only one position or one individual is affected
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will add a subsection making clear that, "Notwithstanding the use of the plural words 'positions,' 'employees,' and 'personnel actions,' this section also applies if the directive ... affects only one position or one individual."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents a narrow grammatical reading from excluding single-position or single-employee moves from the rule's coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive explicitly delineates covered positions, provide list to OPM
rubrics_metrics.description: §302.602(a)(1) states that if the directive explicitly delineates the specific positions that are covered, the agency need only list the positions moved in accordance with that directive, and their location within the organization and provide the list to OPM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM corrected a drafting error to read 'directive' and requires provision of the list to OPM; no additional explanation required beyond the list unless OPM requests it.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive requires selection under directive criteria, provide list and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: §302.602(a)(2) states that if the directive requires the agency to select the positions to be moved pursuant to criteria articulated in the directive, the agency must provide OPM with a list of the positions to be moved, those positions' location in the organization, and, upon request from OPM, an explanation of how the positions met those criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should be prepared to show how listed positions meet the directive's articulated criteria if OPM requests an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive confers discretion to establish objective criteria, provide criteria and relevance explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: §302.602(a)(3) states that where the directive confers discretion on the agency to establish objective criteria for identifying positions or specific slots to move, the agency must supply OPM with the locations in the organization, the objective criteria to be used, and an explanation of how these criteria are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies exercising discretion must be transparent about the objective criteria they will use and justify the relevance of those criteria to the proposed moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice: 30-day written notification to employees in encumbered positions
rubrics_metrics.description: For encumbered positions, under §302.602(c)(1)(i) the agency must provide written notification to the employee of the intent to move the position no less than 30 days prior to moving the position; §302.602(c)(1)(ii) requires that if the move is involuntary the notice must inform the employee that the employee maintains their civil service status and protections notwithstanding the movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice requirement applies when a position is encumbered and is being moved other than into Schedules D or E. OPM clarifies that the involuntary-move notice must state that accrued status and protections continue to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary moves require notice and employee acknowledgement under 5 CFR 302.102(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an employee voluntarily applies for and accepts an excepted service position, agencies must comply with longstanding rules codified at 5 CFR 302.102(b) requiring that employees be given notice that they are leaving the competitive service and requiring that employees acknowledge they understand they are voluntarily leaving the competitive service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves that voluntary acceptance of a new position relinquishes accrued protections; agencies must ensure employees knowingly and voluntarily relinquish rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct MSPB appeal right for involuntary moves that allegedly strip accrued status/right
rubrics_metrics.description: §302.603 prescribes that a competitive service employee whose position is placed into the excepted service involuntarily, or an excepted service employee involuntarily moved to a different schedule, may "directly appeal to the Merit Systems Protection Board" when an entity asserts the move will eliminate accrued status or civil service protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal right does not apply to voluntary acceptance of a new position; it covers allegations that an agency coerced a purportedly voluntary move. OPM added that these appeal rights are "in addition to, and not in derogation of," any other appeal rights under chapter 75 or section 4303. The MSPB will typically assess whether any procedural error was harmful (i.e., likely caused a different outcome) before reversing agency action. Timing and procedural rules follow normal MSPB processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies on successful appeal: correction of notice and compliance with chapter 75/section 4303
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected individual prevails, they may request an order directing the agency (A) to correct the notice to provide that any previously accrued status or procedural and appeal rights continue to apply, and (B) to comply with the requirements of either chapter 75, subchapter II or section 4303 of title 5, in pursuing any action available under those provisions, except to the extent inconsistent with statute (§302.603(b) revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision clarifies the remedial relief available when an agency incorrectly asserts that accrued rights no longer apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals available where agency fails to give required notice or remains silent
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM revised §302.603(c) so that where an agency fails to comply with §302.602(c)(1) and fails to provide the requisite notice, the affected individual may appeal and request an order directing the agency to comply with that provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change addresses concerns that agencies might evade appeals by silence; failure to give required notice is itself appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal can be based on coerced 'voluntary' moves or other involuntary movement
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM added §302.603(d): An individual may appeal on the basis that (A) a facially voluntary move was coerced or otherwise involuntary or (B) a facially voluntary move requiring relinquishment of status was coerced or otherwise involuntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures protection when agencies use coercion or pressure to obtain 'voluntary' relinquishment of accrued protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SES positions excluded from Subpart F; governed by separate statutory structure
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will not include movement of SES positions in Subpart F because the SES "is not in the excepted service and is governed by a separate statutory structure" that addresses access to adverse action protections by appointment type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments asking to include SES positions were rejected; agencies should follow SES-specific statutes and rules for movements/reassignments of career senior executives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural limitations adopted: no required public comment period or 90-day delay
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM declined suggestions to require that personnel actions implementing movements be ineffective until 90 days after release of information to the public or to require a solicitation for public comment on Federal Register publications authorizing moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM considers its publication requirement in the Federal Register sufficient transparency and seeks to balance transparency with operational efficiency; public comment requirement was deemed unduly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of appeals follows normal MSPB procedures (no special filing period prescribed)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will not specify a unique filing period (e.g., proposed 180 days); timing procedures "should instead follow the normal processes associated with appeals to the MSPB."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees should follow existing MSPB procedural timelines and rules when filing appeals under §302.603.
